Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

content adjective

satisfied with what one has

also contented, content with, be content with, make do with

classical

Cic. Sen. 69: eō dēbet esse contentus
Traupman 150, 296

contentus, contenta, contentum

adjective (participle of contineō), with the ablative · Declension on Wiktionary

content, satisfied (with)

From contineō, hold together, hold in: one who keeps within bounds, and so is satisfied with what he has. The same form is also the participle of contendō, stretch, strain: contentus, taut, intent (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • disce parvō esse contentus

    learn to be content with littleSen. Ep. 110.18

  • quod cuique temporis ad vīvendum datur, eō dēbet esse contentus

    whatever time each of us is given to live, with that he ought to be contentCic. Sen. 69

  • nēmō nāscitur dīves; quisquis exit in lūcem jussus est lacte et pannō esse contentus

    no one is born rich: whoever comes into the light is told to be content with milk and a ragSen. Ep. 20.13

  • omnēsque propriīs sunt contentae dōtibus

    and all are content with their own giftsPhaedr. 3.18.10–14

See also happy, enough.
